context_requirements: Intact caspase-3 expression and apoptosome competence (APAF1, cytochrome c release)
Functional apoptotic signaling; TP53 status may modulate but is not strictly required
Cells must not be protected by high BCL2/BCL-XL or IAP overexpression
Activation of executioner caspases in the absence of rapid secondary necrosis
falsifiers: No increase in caspase-3/7 activity or cleaved CASP3/PARP in any cell line at 6 or 24 h
No transcriptional evidence of apoptosis (e.g., no PMAIP1, BAX, or GADD45 induction) at 24 h
Predominant upregulation of proliferation genes rather than downregulation
No difference from vehicle across all nine lines at both time points

evidence.supports: Dapaf-1/Apaf-1 caspase activator is required for cytochrome c-dependent caspase activation and apoptosis
Apaf-1 activates procaspase-9 and is not inhibited by Bcl-2 family prosurvival proteins
Granzyme B is a caspase activator that cleaves pro-caspase-3 to trigger apoptosis
Caspase activator AD-2646 increases cleaved caspase-3/9 and PARP1, confirming pro-apoptotic caspase pathway activation
Cycleanine causes apoptosis via caspase 3/7 activation and PARP cleavage

changes: Removed GADD45A and GADD45B from proximal_up because they are generic stress/DNA-damage response genes, not proximal caspase-activation markers.
Removed GADD45A and GADD45B from late_up because they are generic stress/DNA-damage response genes, not specific apoptosis execution markers.
Removed duplicate GADD45A and GADD45B from late_up to avoid genes appearing in both proximal and late up lists.
Kept CASP3 in late_up as a transcriptional marker of caspase pathway engagement, but noted that caspase activation is primarily post-translational.

Kept BIRC5, CCNB1, CCNA2, CDK1, AURKA, AURKB, PLK1, TOP2A, UBE2C, BUB1B, CDC20, KIF20A, KIF2C, NUSAP1, and MELK in proximal_down as proliferation genes that can be downregulated early during apoptosis.
Kept late_down proliferation genes as expected secondary consequences of caspase-mediated apoptosis.
Kept line_response values as moderate/weak based on general apoptosis sensitivity; no line-specific contradictions were identified from the provided abstracts.
Kept kinetics as slow and magnitude as weak at 6 h and moderate at 24 h, consistent with transcriptional responses to caspase activation.
Kept all evidence citations because their abstracts support the stated claims about caspase activators and apoptosis.
